current_status: As of 2026-09-07, upstream vLLM has never root-caused this failure class, the tooling to do so exists, and two engine defaults changed under it. (1) Unresolved precedent: #19576 (opened 2025-06-12, closed not-planned/stale, v0.8.3 V1, Llama-3.1-8B) - 8 identical benchmark_serving runs against one server, 7 at 220.8-224.2 req/s and one at 191.0 (~15% swing), zero maintainer analysis; #35048 (opened 2026-02-22, closed not-planned/stale) - v0.14.0->v0.15.1 regression, ~19% per-request throughput loss (41.7->33.6 tok/s median) and TTFT p95 +73% (8.7s->15.1s) on 4x/8x H100/H200 TP=4, also closed with no diagnosis. (2) Engine defaults that reshape decode-step variance: async scheduling became the default in v0.14.0 (2026-01, PR #27614, plan #27679, RFC #20727) - CPU-side scheduling overlaps GPU execution, with --no-async-scheduling as the escape hatch (post-release compat fixes: #32701 pipeline parallel, #31679 Qwen3-VL); Model Runner V2 (blog 2026-03-24, opt-in via VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 in the v0.18.0 era, migration #41286) moves per-step input prep (input_ids, positions, query_start_loc, seq_lens) from Python to GPU Triton kernels (+56% throughput Qwen3-0.6B on 1xGB200; 6.3% lower TPOT with MTP spec decode), became default for all models via #53183 by Aug 2026 (in the fork's v0.28.1rc0+23 pin; Q3-2026 roadmap #48168 deprecates MRV1). Note MRV2's GPU-native prep is Triton, which on sm75 hits the FMA-only codegen floor (triton #5066). (3) Determinism machinery: Thinking Machines 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference' (2025-09-10, Horace He) argues atomics are essentially ABSENT from LLM inference forward passes (only FlashAttention backward; Triton avoids atomics via 40%-more-FLOPs recomputation) and names batch-size-dependent numerics (split-K / split-KV reduction order, shape-dependent tiling) as the top drift cause - a correction to the lead as phrased; batch-invariant fixes cost 1.6-2.1x initially (26s->42s/55s, Qwen3-8B 1xGPU); NVLink in-switch reductions are deterministic only on Hopper/Blackwell with CUDA 12.8+. vLLM shipped this as VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (beta; tracking #27433; bitwise train-inference blog 2025-11-10; CI batch-invariant model tests) but requires compute capability >= 8.0 and disables custom all-reduce in TP mode when on. arXiv 2511.17826 (2025-11) extends batch-invariant ops across TP sizes. (4) Profiling methodology: official profiling docs give the nsys recipe (--trace-fork-before-exec=true, --cuda-graph-trace=node, VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn, --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi with --profiler-config.profiler cuda; Proton requires --enforce-eager); #21852 (2025-07-29, V1 vs V0, Llama-4 Maverick 8xH100 NV18) is the canonical cautionary tale: V1's AllReduce kernel time measured 637 ms vs V0's 67 ms with --cuda-graph-trace=node because graph replay charges inter-kernel gaps to the last kernel in the graph - profiler-mode artifact, and NCCL kernel time includes peer-wait (nccl #1747). Red Hat's '5 steps to triage vLLM performance' (2026-03-09) stops at metrics level (TTFT/ITL split, running-vs-waiting, KV/preemption, sequence lengths, nvidia-smi topo -m for PCIe-vs-NVLink TP) and offers no nsys/ncu or variance-statistics guidance. (5) Benchmark protocol: official Benchmark CLI docs warn that repeated vllm bench serve runs reuse prefix-cache entries and inflate throughput - vary --seed or reset/restart the server; vllm bench sweep serve resets /reset_*_cache endpoints between runs; community norm is 3 warmup + 10 measured runs reporting median (SitePoint 2026), discard-first-runs (discussion #7181). Academic grounding: arXiv 2508.10251 (meta-metrics for inference benchmarking), arXiv 2506.09501 (LLM benchmark reproducibility fragility to batch size and GPU count). (6) NCCL: transport and algorithm selection happen once per process at ncclCommInitRank (initTransports in src/transport/p2p.cc; P2P-vs-SHM per rank pair; NCCL_P2P_LEVEL gates by PCIe distance PIX/PXB/PHB/SYS; algorithm/protocol from local tuning tables - deterministic only if every rank sees identical topology, cf. LL128 per-rank mismatch hang nccl #394; surveyed in arXiv 2507.04786 'Demystifying NCCL'). Whether the selection actually flips between restarts on identical single-node hardware is NOT documented anywhere found - the init-time-selection mechanism is real but the per-restart-flip hypothesis is unverified [uncertain]; NCCL_DEBUG=INFO + NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,TUNING logs the per-init choice, and NCCL_ALGO/NCCL_PROTO/NCCL_P2P_LEVEL pin it. (7) Sibling ecosystem: weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (dual 22GB 2080 Ti + NVLink TP=2, vLLM 0.21.0 base) publishes 100+ tok/s single-request decode on Qwen3.6-27B FP8 with MTP3 but no restart-variance methodology at all - nobody in the sm75 ecosystem has published this discipline.
sm75_viability: The phenomenon itself was measured on this host: 2x Quadro RTX 6000 (TU102, sm75) over the NVLink bridge, clocks locked 1455 MHz, CUDA 13.3, driver 610.57.04 - tp1 rows restart-stable (bridge decode 0.99-1.01 across restarts), tp2 decode rows swinging 12.0-17.5 tok/s across engine restarts on both kernel variants (stale 2f1ab8b and tuned HEAD), with within-restart rep spreads bimodal 10.0-15.5 on ctx512_decode, and a stable post-median deficit of 0.85-0.90 vs seeded once 3-restart medians are taken. Locked clocks already remove DVFS as a variable - a methodological asset most public variance reports lack. Instrumentation on Turing: nsys is architecture-agnostic and its CUDA-graph tracing works on sm75; ncu supports Turing for kernel-level replay (detailed per-op counters available on sm75; exact Nsight Compute version matrix under CUDA 13.3 should be smoke-checked first [uncertain]); both ranks of a TP=2 job are traceable in one nsys session with the vLLM-recommended flags; vLLM's built-in torch profiler and Triton Proton (needs --enforce-eager, per-worker rank-qualified output) also run. Capability floors: (a) upstream VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 requires CC >= 8.0, so the flagship determinism machinery is unavailable on sm75 - and its main effect (disabling custom all-reduce in TP) is a TP decode behavior change this host cannot A/B through the flag (would need backport or thinking-machines-lab/batch_invariant_ops, itself Triton-based and FMA-bound on sm75); (b) MRV2's GPU-native input prep runs through Triton kernels that on sm75 compile to FMA-only code (triton #5066, no MMAv1 since Triton 3.3), so the engine-level input-prep cost on Turing is higher than on any documented Ampere+ measurement - a plausible amplifier of per-step CPU/GPU overlap sensitivity under TP2 lockstep; (c) attention-backend matrix for the measurement: BRIDGE_ATTN (fork kernel, CUDA) vs TRITON_ATTN (FMA floor) vs FLEX_ATTENTION - the variance band appears on both BRIDGE and control rows while the control arm stays flat 0.94-1.02, so the swing is not backend-specific. vLLM's custom all-reduce (one/two-shot IPC kernel for small TP messages) is the expected AR path for decode-sized payloads on a 2-GPU NVLink Turing pair; whether it registered on a given restart is checkable from engine logs and is one of the cheap per-restart variables to log. Real blocker summary: nothing prevents the nsys/ncu campaign on sm75; the only sm75-specific hazard is that the upstream determinism features that would substitute for measurement (batch invariance, deterministic NVLS reductions - Hopper/Blackwell only) do not exist on Turing, so the fork must characterize variance statistically rather than eliminate it bitwise.
upstream_base: Dated ledger for engine-level decode-variance instrumentation and its engine-default context: 2025-06-12 #19576 opened (v0.8.3-era V1; ~15% identical-rerun swing; closed not-planned 2025 - the base where the phenomenon was first reported upstream, never diagnosed). 2025-07-29 #21852 opened (v0.9.1, PIECEWISE CUDA-graph V1 default) - established the nsys --cuda-graph-trace=node methodology and the graph-replay attribution artifact for TP AllReduce timing. 2025-09-10 Thinking Machines blog + thinking-machines-lab/batch_invariant_ops. 2025-11-10 vLLM 'Bitwise Consistent Train-Inference' blog; batch-invariance feature lands in vLLM (VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, tracking #27433; CC >= 8.0 floor). 2026-01 v0.14.0: async scheduling default (#27614; --no-async-scheduling added; also the last-good reference point of the #35048 regression window). 2026-02-22 #35048 opened: v0.14.0->v0.15.1 ~19% per-request regression, closed not-planned - versioned-regression precedent showing upstream will not chase this class for you. 2026-03-09 Red Hat 5-step triage article (metrics-level methodology). 2026-03-24 MRV2 blog (v0.18.0-era opt-in VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1; GPU-native input prep). 2026-08 #53183 MRV2 default for all models (Q3-2026 roadmap #48168 deprecating MRV1). Fork pin: 79378fe6e8 = v0.28.1rc0+23, 2026-08-27 - already MRV2-default, so all plan/0007 tp2 decode numbers were taken on the async-scheduling + MRV2 engine; any rebase moves this surface. Batch-invariance doc last updated 2026-08-30.
effort_estimate: Full campaign but instrumentation-led, no new kernels: (1) per-restart environment logging harness (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO + SUBSYS=INIT,TUNING, custom-AR registration line, capture-size list, harness to relaunch the engine N times under the exclusive lease); (2) nsys capture of the tp2 ctx512/ctx2048 decode step, both ranks, >= 3 restarts per kernel variant, in both --cuda-graph-trace=node and graph modes per #21852; (3) timeline extraction and diffing (attention kernel, gather, allreduce/custom-AR durations, inter-kernel gaps, scheduler gaps per decode step) across fast (17.5) vs slow (12.0) restarts; (4) optional ncu pass on the decode-shaped d128 kernel in-engine if nsys re-points at the kernel; (5) cheap discriminator A/Bs that need no profiler: --no-async-scheduling, --disable-custom-all-reduce (or forcing NCCL), pinned NCCL_ALGO/NCCL_PROTO/NCCL_P2P_LEVEL, --enforce-eager (isolates CUDA-graph capture state), each judged by the existing 3-restart median-of-5 protocol with the 5 percent band. Rough size: 3-5 sessions; the gate machinery (cross-restart sampling, rep-spread recording) already landed in plan/0007, so this is analysis plus a small relaunch harness.
unlocks: Every future sub-10-percent delta judgment on this host: the plan/0007 record explicitly holds the macro gate RED on two tp2 bridge decode rows (0.85-0.90 stable deficit) until this campaign explains or recovers the delta, and the same protocol recalibrates all four variance-bound tp2 decode/mixed rows. It unblocks the recorded bisect (per-tile barrier pattern vs stage_now staging width under TP2 lockstep) with evidence instead of conjecture, protects the d=256 deliverable's remaining credibility, and is the methodological prerequisite for the both-card TP=2 NVLink serving target (operator target: Qwen3-class 27B on 2x RTX 6000) - no serving decision made on single-restart numbers is trustworthy until the restart distribution is characterized. It also produces the sm75 engine-variance baseline the sibling ecosystem (weicj fork, ik_llama.cpp) has never published, and tells the fork whether MRV2's Triton-based GPU input prep is a per-step cost hole specific to FMA-floor Turing.
dependency_order: Repo-internal: nothing blocks it - the cross-restart gate (per-row medians across >= 3 restarts) and rep-spread recording landed with plan/0007; the bridge kernel and the 27B engine gate config exist; can start immediately under the exclusive GPU lease. The per-tile barrier/staging bisect (recorded next-campaign follow-up) should consume this campaign's evidence rather than run first - ordering: variance campaign, then bisect. The both-card-tp-nvlink-serving lacuna and w4a16-perf-acceptance depend on trustworthy tp2 numbers and should follow. External prerequisites: nsys and ncu installed under CUDA 13.3 (smoke-check ncu on sm75 first); NCCL debug env vars are runtime switches, no rebuild. Parallelizable: environment-logging and nsys harness are independent; the --no-async-scheduling / custom-AR / NCCL-pin A/B arms can interleave with captures on separate lease windows; profiler-on runs must never feed the timing gates (perturbation), so timing runs and capture runs are strictly separate restarts.
risk_notes: Observer effect is the primary risk: nsys tracing and even torch-profiler overhead perturb the very CPU/GPU overlap being measured, and #21852 proved the cuda-graph-trace mode itself changes AllReduce attribution by up to 570 ms on a large run (graph replay charges inter-kernel gaps to the last kernel) - so captures must be treated as structural evidence (where does time go) and never as timing evidence (how much end-to-end); NCCL kernel duration includes peer-wait, so a 'slow allreduce' can actually be a slow producer on the other rank (nccl #1747). Misattribution risks: pinning NCCL env vars changes the baseline being measured (report both pinned and unpinned); --no-async-scheduling is not the shipped configuration, so findings there must be revalidated on defaults; --enforce-eager removes CUDA graphs entirely and changes decode performance character. Numerics risk is low - this campaign changes no kernel and the float64-oracle gates already hold - but conclusions feed the barrier/staging bisect, so a wrong localization compounds. Upstream-drift exposure: the surface sits on two freshly-defaulted engine subsystems (async scheduling 2026-01, MRV2 2026-08) with active churn (#48168 deprecating MRV1), so findings age quickly across rebases; NCCL tuning tables are version-dependent. Silent-fallback hazard specific to sm75: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT silently requires CC >= 8.0 and custom-AR behavior differs when enabled - neither available/active on Turing, so any upstream determinism fix upstream merges will not transfer without porting. The stable 0.85-0.90 deficit could also be genuinely kernel-interaction (barrier pattern under lockstep) rather than pure engine noise - the campaign must keep that hypothesis alive rather than explain everything away as variance.
determinism_class: Two distinct classes must be kept separate, and the leads partially conflated them. Class A - numerics determinism (bitwise vs statistical): Thinking Machines (2025-09-10) shows atomics are essentially absent from inference forward passes and the top numerics drift driver is batch-size-dependent reduction order (split-K, split-KV, shape-dependent tiling); their atomic-free deterministic substitutes (split/tree reductions with sequential clean-up, semaphores, fixed split-size attention) cost 1.6-2.1x initially; deterministic NVLink in-switch reductions exist only on Hopper/Blackwell with CUDA 12.8+, so Turing TP allreduce numerics stay statistical. The fork's float64-oracle + median-of-N discipline already covers Class A on the kernel lane; VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT cannot be used on sm75 (CC >= 8.0). Class B - performance determinism (this lacuna): restart-to-restart throughput variance is statistical by nature and the oracle gate is irrelevant to it; what must hold is the sampling contract already recorded in plan/0007 - per-restart median of 5 in-process reps, >= 3 restarts, medians within a 5 percent band before sub-10-percent deltas are interpreted. Ranked restart-state variables by current evidence [uncertain ranking - this is hypothesis, to be settled by the campaign]: (1) per-step CPU/GPU scheduling overlap state under TP2 lockstep (async-scheduling default since v0.14.0 amplifies sensitivity to launch-timing phase; MRV2 GPU-native prep is Triton-FMA-slow on sm75, widening the per-step prep window); (2) CUDA-graph capture state per restart (captured size list, padding bucket, memory-pool addresses chosen at capture time); (3) NCCL communicator init-time selection - transport (P2P vs SHM), algorithm, protocol, channel count fixed once per restart; the init-time-selection mechanism is documented (initTransports, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL) but an actual flip between restarts on identical single-node hardware is undocumented [uncertain]; (4) custom all-reduce registration vs NCCL fallback per restart; (5) atomics - NOT implicated for engine throughput variance (per Thinking Machines), and the fork's split-K atomicAdd accumulation issue is a separate lacuna (cuda-graph-atomic-reduction) about numerics across graph replays, not tok/s. The signature to exploit: tp1 restart-stable vs tp2 swinging implicates the TP interaction surface (gather/allreduce/lockstep scheduling) rather than the attention inner loop, which the kernel-isolated A/B already exonerated (tuned 2324/2176 us vs stale 2523 us per launch).
priority_signal: For: plan/0007 explicitly names this the next campaign and holds the macro gate RED on two rows until it runs - it is the only item blocking closure of a delivered objective's final verdict; every later perf judgment on this host (w4a16 acceptance, both-card serving, paged decode) inherits its protocol or inherits noise; upstream demonstrably will not do it (#19576 and #35048 both closed not-planned without diagnosis - the fork must self-serve); the instrument (nsys/ncu) is cheap, Turing-supported, and already half-built on the plan/0007 gate machinery; locked clocks make the host unusually good for this class of measurement. The stable 0.85-0.90 post-median deficit is a real 10-15 percent TP2 decode cost on the operator's target topology - likely the highest-value single unexplained number on the board. Against: it is instrumentation and methodology, not a new capability - no artifact beyond a protocol and a diagnosis; the window is not closing (the variance will still be there next quarter), though the engine surface churns (MRV2 default landed inside the fork pin in Aug 2026, so every rebase re-validates the phenomenon against a moving base); part of the deliverable (restart-median protocol) already shipped with plan/0007, so the marginal ask is specifically the nsys/ncu localization of the 0.85-0.90 deficit; and there is a temptation risk the campaign 'explains' a deficit that is actually the barrier/staging bisect's to fix - the boundary must be kept empirical.
recommended_probe: Gate-0 discipline: no timing conclusions until the instrument is validated, and captures never feed the timing gates. Step 0 (validate instrument, ~1 hour): smoke nsys on the existing 27B TP=2 engine with the official flags (--trace-fork-before-exec=true, --cuda-graph-trace=node, VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn) and smoke ncu on the sm75 bridge kernel standalone. Step 1 (cheapest discriminator, no profiler - run first): across 6 engine restarts of the SAME kernel build, log per restart: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO + NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,TUNING output (transport, algo, proto, channels), custom-all-reduce registration line, captured graph size list, and ctx512_decode median-of-5; then A/B single variables with 3 restarts each: --no-async-scheduling, custom-AR disabled (force NCCL), NCCL_ALGO/NCCL_PROTO pinned, --enforce-eager. If the 12.0-17.5 swing collapses under any pin, the per-restart variable is found for free and only the stable 0.85-0.90 deficit remains. Step 2 (nsys localization): capture the tp2 ctx512_decode steady state on BOTH ranks for one fast (~17 tok/s) and one slow (~12 tok/s) restart, node-trace mode primary with a graph-mode cross-check per #21852; extract per-decode-step attention kernel, gather, allreduce/custom-AR durations and inter-kernel gaps; the deficit must localize into scheduler gaps, AR wait, or kernel time - each points to a different fix (scheduling overlap, transport/AR path, barrier/staging bisect). Step 3 (ncu only if nsys re-points at the kernel): replay the decode-shaped d128 instantiation in-engine and compare against the isolated 2324 us number. Judgment contract throughout: per-restart median-of-5, >= 3 restarts per arm, 5 percent band; oracle gates untouched; all findings recorded as restart distributions, never single captures.
